newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hyundai Group aims for 14 pct sales rise.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hyundai Group aims for 14 pct sales rise.

text.p: South Korea's Hyundai Group aims to boost sales by 14 percent this year, but analysts said the yen's weakness and an uncertain outlook for the computer chip sector could make the target hard to achieve.

Hyundai, the biggest South Korean conglomerate in terms of assets, said on Tuesday the combined sales target for its 50 units had been set at 80 trillion won ($92.2 billion) this year, against an estimated 70 trillion won in 1996.

"(All member companies) should do their best to promote exports, reduce material costs and improve productivity," a group spokesman quoted chairman Chung Mong-koo as saying during a recent executives' meeting.
Revenue breakdowns by company were not given.
Hyundai units count among the world's top manufacturing firms, including carmaker Hyundai Motor Co, chipmaker Hyundai Electronics Industries Co and shipbuilder Hyundai Heavy Industries Co.
Hyundai aims to boost exports by its member firms to $17.3 billion from $15.2 billion in 1996.
But analysts said a weak Japanese yen could throw a wrench into the group's plan.

"The yen's value is a very important factor for Hyundai, as it is for the national economy. In particular, a weaker yen will make it hard for Hyundai to expand its car and ship exports," said Shim Choong-bo, research manager at Daishin Securities.
A soft yen makes Japanese products relatively cheaper in overseas markets, where South Korean exporters compete fiercely in many major items with the Japanese.
The yen has recently been trading at four-year lows of just over 122 yen per dollar and economists have forecast the trend would persist through the first half of this year.
Last year's free-falling international prices for computer memory chips has also been a major hurdle for Hyundai's exports.

Hyundai Electronics, among the world's top-five suppliers of memory chips, earlier announced a goal of expanding this year's sales of chips and electronic appliances to 4.1 trillion won from an estimated 3.2 trillion won in 1996.
"The goal is based on forecasts that the price of 16-megabit chips will rebound to around $10 by year-end (from about $8 at present)," a spokesman for Hyundai Electronics said.
But he declined to comment when asked whether the company should revise the sales target down if the outlook for memory chip prices looked bleak.
Hyundai Group plans to increase investment in production facilities and in research and development projects to nine trillion won from an estimated 8.2 trillion won in 1996.

In an effort to streamline production, it will abandon some manufacturing operations valued at 41.73 billion won in annual sales and instead purchase needed items from non-member firms. ($1 = 867.80 won)
